businessProfile.productSummary: A direct-to-consumer trial/intro offer for a consumer FMCG (likely a wellness, beauty, or functional beverage) aimed at younger adults willing to 'try' new products.
businessProfile.brandVoice: casual/playful — low-friction, try-it-now messaging (inferred from the 'just try it' prompt)

assumptions: The advertiser is selling a consumer packaged product (FMCG) rather than a service or B2B product.
The specific vertical is wellness/beauty/functional beverage (chosen because 'just try it' implies a trialable consumable).
Pricing is mid-tier, with an estimated AOV around $35–55 (a typical trial/subscription entry price).
Goal is to drive trial sign-ups or first-time purchases rather than enterprise sales or purely awareness.
clarifyingQuestions: What exactly is the product category (beauty, beverage, supplement, pet product, apparel, etc.)?
What is your target audience (age, gender, regions) and primary campaign goal — trials, subscriptions, or one-time purchases?
What is the expected price point / AOV and do you offer a subscription after trial?
What creative assets do you have (video, lifestyle imagery, scientific/ingredient claims) and any regulatory constraints?

reasons: Category match: Velvetline is a DTC beauty publisher (skews to Gen Z/younger millennials) — an ideal audience for sample/trial beauty products.
Audience fit: Velvetline's 18-34 skew and 91% female audience aligns with trial-focused beauty buyers who discover via lifestyle channels.
AOV compatibility: Velvetline's avg_order_value $61 is close to the assumed mid AOV (≈$45), supporting trial-to-full-purchase conversion.
Notes alignment: Minimalist/aesthetic-driven purchasing on Velvetline matches a casual 'try it' brand voice.
Category match: Pop & Sip specializes in functional beverages and gut-health drinks — direct fit if the product is a functional beverage.
Audience fit: 22-42 skew and wellness-curious audience maps to trial buyers of new functional drinks.
AOV match: Pop & Sip's $42 AOV closely matches the assumed trial price point.
Notes alignment: Pop & Sip's overlap with wellness and premium grocery supports sampling and subscription upsell.
Category match: Daily Form is wellness_dtc (vitamins/supplements) and is built for trial-and-subscription models.
Audience fit: 22-42, highly female audience that prefers science-backed claims — useful if the trial needs credibility.
Notes alignment: Daily Form's 'science-forward' audience will convert better if advertiser provides ingredient/transparency claims.
Category match: Strandlab focuses on personalized beauty/haircare and uses quiz-based onboarding — good for trial-to-subscription flows.
Audience fit: 18-38 skew (personalization-motivated) who respond to sample offers and quizzes that reduce friction.
Notes alignment: Strandlab's onboarding approach can lift conversions for a 'try it' product that benefits from personalization.
Audience & intent: Kitchenly (meal kits) reaches convenience-motivated households nationwide and can be a strong channel for edible/consumable trials aimed at families/couples.
Scale & AOV: Kitchenly's large impression volume and $74 AOV supports both trial and subscription upsell for food/beverage adjacent products.
Notes alignment: Audience is food-interested and convenience-motivated — receptive to try-now offers that reduce effort.
Purchase behavior: Swiftcart drives high-frequency, impulse purchases (instant delivery/convenience) — good for trial or sample-size, low-friction buys.
Audience fit: 18-34 skew and late-night impulse traffic supports a casual 'just try it' positioning targeting quick conversions.
AOV compatibility: Swiftcart's $28 AOV fits lower-end trials or add-on purchases to increase trial distribution.

excludedPublishers.reason: Movewell is an activewear apparel publisher (female fitness apparel, subscription clothing) — it does not primarily support beauty/beverage trial purchases.
Studiogrid sells appointment-based wellness services (fitness classes, spa) where trialing a consumable product is not the primary commerce behavior.
Marlowe & Co. targets older affluent women (45-65) with high-AOV workwear; its audience buys less on impulse and is less likely to be the early-trial cohort for a youth-oriented 'try it' product.
Linden Park is a high-AOV classic apparel publisher skewing 50-70; its conservative shoppers are unlikely to be the primary early adopters for an experimental trial FMCG.
Everbody focuses on inclusive women's apparel and fit messaging, not on DTC consumable trials — category mismatch for a beauty/beverage/supplement trial.
Pawline is pet-focused (pet food/subscription) and while pet owners buy consumables, it's specialized toward pet health rather than human-focused beauty/beverage trials.

Pantrygood specializes in organic grocery shoppers with a high-income skew focused on pantry/subscriptions; while related, its shoppers expect established grocery SKUs rather than small DTC trial offers unless the product is packaged grocery-grade.
Ruffco is the largest pet audience in the catalog (repeat pet purchases) and is not appropriate unless the product is pet-specific.
Heartfoot is a basics/gifting apparel publisher where the primary purchase behavior is apparel gifting, not consumable sample trials.
Northbed is high-AOV home textiles where shoppers are design-conscious and purchase infrequently; poor match for low-AOV trial FMCG offers.
Hearthstone Goods targets high-AOV cookware/kitchen shoppers buying durable goods, not trial-size consumables.
Stride & Stem is premium sustainable shoes for professional women (high AOV); not a commerce environment for consumable trials.
Cloudfoot focuses on sustainable footwear/active shoes (comfort + sustainability); its purchase intent is apparel/shoes rather than consumable trials.
Tailcrate is a pet supplies/toys subscription publisher centered on playful pet products — relevant only if the advertised trial is pet-focused.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Wellness Optimizer (28-40, female) actively tries science-backed wellness products and pays for evidence-based trials; aligns with Daily Form and Pop & Sip audiences.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Clinically-formulated trial sized for measurable benefits — try a risk-free sample backed by transparent ingredients and outcomes.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Gen Z Aesthete discovers through visual lifestyle channels and loves aesthetic-forward, novel trial products — matches Velvetline and Strandlab audiences.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Limited-run, Instagram-ready trial — look good, feel new; try a small pack that fits your vibe.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Convenience-First Millennial values speed and low friction and will convert on easy, fast trials — aligns with Swiftcart and Kitchenly placements.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Get a trial delivered fast with one-click checkout and easy subscription opt-in/opt-out.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Fitness Enthusiast will sample performance-focused consumables (functional beverages or supplements) and respond to performance claims — good fit for Pop & Sip and Daily Form.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Performance-supporting formula optimized for workouts — try a sample and feel the difference in recovery/energy.

variants.headline: Trial-size sample with full ingredient transparency
variants.body: Get a trial-size sample with a complete ingredient list and clear usage guidance so you can track any changes. Short, low-commitment pack designed to let you measure effects and decide if it fits your regimen.
variants.rationale: Focuses on ingredient transparency and measurable outcomes to appeal to a data-driven wellness optimizer who avoids hype.

variants.headline: Limited-run, Instagram-ready trial pack
variants.body: A small, photo-ready sample in distinctive packaging—perfect for your feed. Includes a brief brand note so you know what the product stands for; try it, style it, and decide if the vibe fits you.
variants.rationale: Leans on visual packaging, limited availability, and brand values to match the Gen Z Aesthete's emphasis on aesthetic and identity.

variants.headline: One-click trial — fast delivery and easy subscription
variants.body: Order a trial in one tap, get a small pack shipped fast, and opt into a subscription from your account with a single toggle. Try it now—quick checkout, fast arrival, simple subscription control.
variants.rationale: Highlights speed, one-click checkout, and effortless subscription opt-in/opt-out to match a convenience-first millennial's expectations.

variants.headline: Training-friendly sample — try it for recovery & energy
variants.body: Small sample formulated for workouts so you can test post-session recovery and steady energy for yourself. Use it around training days and judge how it fits your performance routine before committing.
variants.rationale: Emphasizes workout relevance and self-testing of recovery/energy without overclaiming, aligning with a performance-focused fitness buyer.

bidStrategy.rationale: Mid-AOV product: pay per click at 1-2% of order value, a sustainable CPC if roughly 1 in 30 clicks converts

budget.rationale: $1500/publisher/month floor for statistically useful volume × 5 publishers × 1 mid-tier multiplier
